title: PSICOPEDAGOGIA INSTITUCIONAL E CLÍNICA: AVALIAÇÃO E INTERVENÇÃO EM DIFICULDADES DE APRENDIZAGEM
desc: Este artigo analisa as contribuições da Psicopedagogia Institucional e Clínica na avaliação e intervenção diante das dificuldades de aprendizagem. O estudo caracteriza-se como uma pesquisa qualitativa, exploratória e descritiva, desenvolvida por meio de pesquisa bibliográfica e documental, utilizando o método dedutivo e análise temática das fontes selecionadas. A investigação aborda aspectos relacionados à identificação das dificuldades, aos procedimentos de avaliação psicopedagógica, ao planejamento das intervenções e à articulação entre profissionais, família e instituição escolar. Os resultados indicam que as dificuldades de aprendizagem apresentam manifestações diversificadas e não devem ser interpretadas exclusivamente a partir do baixo desempenho acadêmico. A avaliação precisa considerar o histórico do estudante, suas habilidades preservadas, as características cognitivas, as experiências escolares e as condições que envolvem o processo de aprendizagem. Verificou-se também a importância de diferenciar dificuldades escolares de transtornos específicos da aprendizagem, evitando conclusões precipitadas e intervenções inadequadas. A Psicopedagogia Clínica possibilita acompanhamento individualizado, enquanto a atuação institucional favorece ações preventivas e análise das condições educacionais. Conclui-se que a intervenção psicopedagógica apresenta melhores possibilidades de resultados

Data Management Plan AQUASERV PID: 37027 MICROMIX - Interaction between microplastics and mercury in a benthic microcosm
desc: Microplastics (MP) and mercury (Hg) are ubiquitous environmental pollutants with known adverse effects on organisms. In aquatic environments, their co-occurrence and properties promote interactions, which can alter the environmental fate, bioavailability and toxicity of both contaminants. This project aims to investigate the ecotoxicological impacts of MP-Hg interactions on benthic ecosystems through  in vivo microcosm exposures of bivalves ( Macoma balthica ) in the presence of Hg-resistant microbial communities in the sediment. The objectives are to assess mercury speciation, bioaccumulation, toxicity biomarkers and gut microbiome. The expected outcomes are new insights on the interactions of MP-Hg and on their toxicological and ecological impact on benthic ecosystems. This data can contribute to the improvement of environmental risk assessment and management strategies. This DMP describes the management of chemical speciation, biochemical and metagenomic data generated throughout the project. It ensures compliance with the FAIR principles and AQUASERV open access requirements.

title: Impact and characteristics of oxygen vacancies in ferroelectric HfO2 based materials
desc: This Data Management Plan (DMP) has been developed for the project "Impact and characteristics of oxygen vacancies in ferroelectric HfO₂ based materials." The project investigates the concentration, spatial distribution, charge state, coordination number, and activation energies of oxygen vacancies in undoped and doped hafnia-based materials, as well as their influence on the structural, ferroelectric, and electrical properties of bulk materials and thin films. The research involves extensive experimental work, including microwave-assisted and hydrothermal synthesis, thin-film fabrication, and advanced characterization techniques such as X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), thermoluminescence (TL), photoluminescence (PL), electron microscopy (SEM/TEM), piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM), dielectric and electrical measurements, and synchrotron-based EXAFS spectroscopy. The purpose of this DMP is to ensure that all research data are systematically collected, documented, organized, stored, and preserved throughout the project lifecycle. The plan establishes procedures that comply with the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable), promoting research transparency, reproducibility, and long-term usability of the generated datasets. It also supports compliance with the data management policies of the Institute of Solid State Physics, University of Latvia (ISSP UL), and the funding agency while facilitating open science through the publication of datasets, metadata, and related research outputs in trusted repositories such as Zenodo whenever possible.

title: DMP for Fundamental and Applied Research Project "Novel source towards challenging monofluorocarbene" (No. lzp-2024/1-0309)
desc: Fluorohalomethanes as the most common sources of fluorocarbenes and carbenoids are often low-boiling, have limited availability, and are environmentally unfriendly, leading to their regulation under the Montreal Protocol. On the other hand, carboxylic acid fluorohalomethyl esters show great potential as feasible precursors for a fluorocarbene species to access valuable monofluorinated compounds. Such novel source to fluorocarbenes would offer not only small ring formation via cycloadditions, but also σ-bond (N-H, Si-H, P-H, B-H, S-H, C-C) insertions and potentially cross-couplings. This approach would offer a freon-free source of reactive and catalyst tunable monofluorocarbene intermediates with potentially diverse range of otherwise inaccessible chemistry due to nonexistent fluorodiazomethane. The aim of the project is to develop a novel fluorocarbene transfer reagent based on carbonyl or sulfoniums salt precursors and explore its application in synthesis of new fluorinated building blocks. This will be achieved by following objectives: Development and synthesis of novel fluorocarbene source – carboxylic acid fluorohalomethyl ester or fluorhalomethyl sulfonium salt as a synthetic equivalent of CHF synthon. Improved synthetic methodology exploiting novel fluorocarbene source to obtain fluorinated small rings, X-H and C-C insertions, fluorocarbene cross-coupling products. Validation of developed methodology on biologically significant drug molecules via indroduction of fluorinated bioisosters.

desc: El programa de Metodología de la Investigación , correspondiente a la Maestría en Administración y Dirección Estratégica de la División Académica de Ciencias Económico-Administrativas, se impartirá en el ciclo agosto-diciembre de 2026. Su propósito es fortalecer las competencias para analizar, seleccionar y justificar métodos, enfoques, alcances y diseños de investigación aplicables a los problemas de las ciencias económico-administrativas. A lo largo del curso, los participantes trabajarán en la delimitación del tema, el planteamiento del problema, la formulación de preguntas, objetivos, hipótesis o supuestos y la construcción de una matriz de congruencia metodológica. Asimismo, aplicará los principios de la escritura académica y el estilo APA, séptima edición, para elaborar citas, referencias, tablas, figuras y textos científicos. Mediante estrategias sistematizadas de búsqueda bibliográfica, selección documental y revisión de la literatura, integrará un corpus académico y desarrollará un marco teórico argumentado. El producto final será un protocolo de investigación congruente, sustentado y presentado mediante un portafolio digital de evidencias de carácter científico.

title: Optimization of prophylactic antibacterial therapy in spinal surgery through mechanical PKPD modelling to reduce the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria (OPATS-PKPD)
desc: The objective of the project is to develop a mechanism-based model to optimize cefazolin therapy in patients undergoing discectomy. This model will integrate the study of how the drug moves through the body, how it interacts with bacteria, and statistical simulations to predict the best dosing strategies. By analyzing clinical data, including cefazolin concentrations in both blood plasma and intervertebral discs, the project aims to improve treatment effectiveness, enhance patient safety, and reduce the risk of bacteria developing resistance. The hypothesis will be tested through a final analysis of drug behavior in a group of patients receiving optimized therapy. Additionally, by incorporating data on drug distribution, bacterial response, and patient variability, the project will determine how well the antibiotic reaches its target in the intervertebral disc and establish an improved treatment protocol for better patient outcomes.

title: Development of structure and data-driven methods for analysis and control of complex dynamical systems
desc:
Recent decades have been marked by giant transformations that created enormous opportunities in different fields of technology and science. One of the signs of these transformations is the overwhelming volume of data produced. Leveraging this data is the key to the next-generation technologies. While there has been substantial progress in developing advanced machine learning algorithms, the use of mathematical structures, inherent to many technical and technological processes can not only substantially increase the quality of the used algorithms, but also provide additional insight and give an impetus to the further development of data-driven methods. We aim to follow this direction by developing novel, data- and structure-driven approaches for the modeling of complex technical systems and using the obtained models for designing the control laws. The novelty of this project is twofold:
 1.	A unique interplay between the analytical, differential-geometric methods and elaborated numerical schemes, which are consistent with the underlying geometrical structure of the systems under study.
 2.	A systematic development and joint application of theoretical, Koopman operator-based, and numerical, machine learning-based methods within the control-theoretic framework.

title: Disempowering John Chrysostom: Bodily, Emotional, and Gender Vulnerability in the Letters to Women
desc: Paper presented at the Second International Post-Graduate Conference of the GCLA, "Vulnerability and Power in Late Antiquity (4th-9th centuries)", University of Ghent, Ghent (27-28-29 April 2026)   Abstract This paper examines John Chrysostom’s exile letters to women as a source for investigating how power – political, ecclesiastical, and patriarchal – handled vulnerability in Late Antiquity. When Emperor Arcadius removed him from the episcopal see of Constantinople (404 CE), John found his position of power compromised. Effectively, he lost any control over Church affairs and contact with the court, being relegated to a desolate, inhospitable spot between Cappadocia and Armenia – Cucusus. John’s letters from that period, and especially those addressed to women, depict the exiled bishop as vulnerable to physical and psychological ailments. In his correspondence with the deaconess Olympias and in that with the noblewoman Theodora (e.g., Epp. 4, 6, 13, 120 Migne), for instance, Chrysostom insistently complains about the illnesses contracted while in exile (including fevers, vomiting, and insomnia), in addition to the distress over the local marauders’ attacks. Overall, John describes his own (old) body as worn-out. Alternatively, a sort of ‘emotional’ vulnerability emerges from some letters to other women (e.g., Epp. 33, 98, 185), where the author expresses his grief due to loneliness (ἐρημία), but also the despondency (ἀθυμία) caused by his addressees’ poor health. title: SHIFT: Shaping Informed Frameworks for Trust
desc:
SHIFT (Shaping Informed Frameworks for Trust) is an EU-funded Preparatory Action under call CNECT/2024/1917981 — European Narratives Observatory to fight Disinformation, coordinated by the Center for the Study of Democracy (CSD) and running from April 2026 for 18 months across 13 countries: 12 EU Member States and Moldova (BG, SK, CZ, MD, PL, DE, RO, DK, IE, LV, EE, LT, FR). The consortium brings together public policy research institutes, behavioural communication specialists, civic tech innovators, and NGOs: CSD, GLOBSEC, Alliance4Europe, CeMAS, Funky Citizens, Logiq Media, European Movement Ireland, Rīga Stradiņš University, and Make.org, with supporting engagement from the Thomson Reuters Foundation. SHIFT builds the missing link in Europe's response to disinformation: going beyond detecting harmful narratives to testing what works to counter them. It combines cross-national research, audience segmentation, and real-world campaign testing to understand what works to counter disinformation and why. SHIFT addresses a critical gap in Europe’s response to disinformation: moving beyond detection and debunking to understand what actually works to counter it. The project examines how harmful narratives shape beliefs, trust and behaviour across different audiences, with the aim of identifying effective, evidence-based strategies to mitigate their impact.
 S HIFT combines cross-national survey research, digital ecosystem analysis and behavioural audience segmentation to map how disinformation operates as a system of influence. title: Dynamic Impedance-enabled Gut-on-chip for Epithelial Sensing and Therapy modeling
desc: DIGEST develops the first organ-on-chip platform that combines full-spectrum impedance sensing and true anaerobic culturing within continuous dynamic flow conditions, unlocking real-time insight into gut cell barrier failure. This leap enables what others cannot: automated, precise, long-term modelling and monitoring of gut cell cultures in flow. Validated using personalized diseased gut models, the platform will offer a uniquely human-relevant testbed that outperforms static and PDMS-based systems, replaces animal testing, and cuts preclinical R&D costs by up to 26%, accelerating therapy development for Crohn’s and Ulcerative Colitis, or their intestinal diseases. Inflammatory bowel diseases, including Crohn’s and Ulcerative Colitis, are rising sharply and often remain resistant to treatments. By 2030, over 7 million people in Europe and the U.S. are expected to be affected. Yet researchers still rely on outdated models that fail to capture the complexity of the human gut for drug development. This project delivers a next-generation organ-on-chip platform, combining dynamic flow with TEER, pH and oxygen sensing, to model disease progression and treatment response with precision. By replacing animal testing and accelerating breakthroughs, we aim to improve therapy outcomes and bring hope to millions living with these diseases.

desc: The project generates both raw and processed research data. Raw data include individual fish body weight and total length measurements, tank biomass at each sampling occasion, mortality records, and digital images of individual fish collected at each sampling point for non-invasive image-based identification. Com recurso a um referencial teórico alinhado na abordagem sensível ao trauma ou  Trauma-Informed, baseado no Modelo Experiencial, propõe-se o desenvolvimento de um programa de formação a aplicar em casa de acolhimento  residencial, envolvendo todos os adultos cuidadores da casa de acolhimento (equipa técnica e diretor técnico, equipa educativa e de apoio).  Posteriormente, será realizada a avaliação do impacto deste programa- piloto e conduzido um estudo quasi-experimental com follow-up de 3 meses  para testar a eficácia do programa desenvolvido. Como principal produto espera-se obter um programa baseado na evidência com impacto na  mudança das práticas dos cuidadores, mais responsivos e autorregulados emocionalmente, e diminuição das estratégias disciplinares punitivas e  violadoras de direitos, melhoria de indicadores de ajustamento psicológico em crianças e adolescentes acolhidos.  O Plano de Gestão de Dados será elaborado de acordo com as boas práticas científicas, os princípios FAIR, e as orientações da ciência aberta, a fim de garantir a transparência, a acessibilidade e a reutilização dos dados do projet

title: AQUASERV example DMP
desc: **** Example DMP **** This TNA project is a short field-to-lab survey of rocky-shore rockpools aimed at documenting biodiversity patterns and basic water properties across multiple coastal locations. Samples/observations will be collected from ~10 rockpools along a defined shoreline transect, with each site assigned a unique Pool ID. For each pool, geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude) and contextual information (date/time, site notes) will be recorded, and simple environmental measurements will be taken using handheld sensors (e.g., water temperature in °C, salinity in PSU, maximum depth in m). The project will generate two main datasets: (1) a structured spreadsheet containing sampling event metadata, georeferenced measurements, and species occurrence records linked to each Pool ID; and (2) a set of digital images (context photos and organism photos) captured per pool, named using a consistent convention and linked to the spreadsheet via Pool ID and image identifiers. Species names will be standardized using an authoritative taxonomy (e.g., WoRMS with AphiaIDs), and measurement variables will be recorded with clear units and controlled terms to support reuse, integration, and publication in relevant repositories.

title: PID2020-112967GB-C32 - Meeting Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Rail Passenger Service Planning under Competition.
desc: This Data Management Plan (DMP) describes the strategy for managing, storing, sharing and preserving the research outputs generated within the project PID2020-112967GB-C32 “Meeting Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Rail Passenger Service Planning under Competition”, funded by the Spanish State Research Agency (AEI). The project aims to develop mathematical models, machine learning methods and artificial intelligence techniques to support tactical and operational decision making in liberalized railway passenger markets. Research activities include demand forecasting, transport mode choice modelling, railway timetable and pricing optimization, reinforcement learning, simulation of competitive railway markets and the development of optimization and machine learning software. The project will generate research software, simulation environments, machine learning models, numerical experiment results and datasets derived from simulations or publicly available transport data. The DMP establishes how these research outputs will be documented, stored, shared and preserved according to the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable).

title: The Risk Management Implementation For Industry 4.0
desc: Abstract The fourth industrial revolution heralds a new age of production. While previous industrial revolutions were characterized by steam power, electrification, and early computer tech- nologies, Industry 4.0 represents the complete digital transformation of the manufacturing industry [1]. This new generation uses the digital reality, AI, cloud, and IoT which are combined in the operation and maintenance ....etc. Industry 4.0 focuses on the increase of the efficiency of managing the production processes. However, there are some risks in implementing the Industry 4.0 such as modified frameworks, more complex IT infrastruc- ture and so on, new types of risks may occur [2]. In many cases, the implementation of Industry 4.0 has shown that the connections between humans, systems and objects have become a more complex, dynamic and real-time optimized network [2]. On the other hand, there is the fact of data volume and availability enhancement in real time which causes new requirements of the infrastructure, management, technologies..etc. In this paper we will present a comprehensive literature review on the implementation challenges and risk management approaches in Industry 4.0. The review examines key technological compo- nents, adoption barriers, and emerging risk mitigation strategies through analysis of recent scholarly publications. The findings highlight critical gaps in current research and suggest directions for future work in this domain.

title: PID:42107-Sinéad Cahill-PhD-AQUASERV-DMP
desc: Seagrass ecosystems are considered key blue carbon sinks due to their capacity to store particulate organic carbon in the sediments. However, other mechanisms of carbon sequestration remain understudied, such as outwelling or export of recalcitrant dissolved carbon. This project aims to unravel these pathways through the study of how theseecosystems influence the seawater carbonate system in present and future climatic conditions. Using advanced instrumentation at Kristineberg Centre—Picarro gas analysers, automatic alkalinity titrators, spectrophotometers, and nutrient analysis facilities— together with in situ field measurements in nearby meadows; the study will assess fluxes of multiple carbon species and greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O). Results will determine whether these ecosystems act as carbon sinks or sources. Expected outcomes include improved understanding of the role of seagrasses in coastal carbon budgets and guidance for their inclusion in climate mitigation strategies.

desc: This is the final version of PIISA's Risk and Ethics guide. title: Data Management Plan for POSTDOC Project on Chaos-Secured Data Transmission for Power Grid Inspection
desc: This Data Management Plan describes the management, documentation, storage, access, preservation and re-use of research data generated and processed within the postdoctoral research project “Chaos-Based Data Transmission for Power Grid Inspection: Enhancing Cyber-Physical Security in Energy Networks”. The project will use and generate several categories of research outputs, including UAV-based RGB and LiDAR inspection data, synthetic and benchmark image data, MATLAB-based chaos modulation models, simulation code, encrypted and decrypted image transmission outputs, performance evaluation metrics, digital twin integration documentation, technical reports and publication-related datasets. The DMP follows FAIR principles by ensuring that suitable research outputs are findable through structured metadata and persistent identifiers, accessible through trusted repositories where possible, interoperable through open and well-documented formats, and reusable through clear licensing, versioning and documentation. Data that may disclose sensitive information about power grid infrastructure, operational inspection workflows, geographic locations, security configurations or non-public industrial information will be subject to restricted access, anonymisation, aggregation or replacement with synthetic data before publication.

title: 41884_Exploring_seagrass_meadows_as_local_climate_change_refugia
desc:
This project examines how natural diel variability in pH and dissolved oxygen, driven by the seagrass Zostera marina , affects the physiology and ecological performance of benthic calcifying organisms under ocean warming. Experiments will be conducted in outdoor mesocosms at the Kristineberg Center, using different seagrass densities to simulate constant versus fluctuating environmental conditions combined with warming and acidified treatments. The project will generate:
 -	High-frequency environmental data (pH, oxygen, temperature).
 -	Biological and physiological data (e.g., survival, growth, calcification). -	Experimental metadata and analytical outputs (processed datasets and R scripts).
 These data will support scientific publications and improve understanding of how vegetated habitats may buffer climate-related stressors.

title: MobiMad@PT
desc:
Medication non-adherence is a critical challenge for global health systems, with evidence suggesting that up to half of patients may not follow their prescribed medication. Given the rates of medication non-adherence and its detrimental effects on health outcomes and health systems sustainability, numerous Dose Administration Aids (DAA) interventions have been developed. Most of them are packaging and dosage modifications, either in single and manually prepared dosette boxes, or in multidose automated dispensing (MAD) systems, prepared in community or hospital pharmacies. However, in spite of their success, most MAD are cumbersome and lack long-term sustainability.
 In an era where digital health technologies are reshaping healthcare delivery, this project introduces Mobili® in Portugal, a portable MAD systemdeveloped by the Norwegian start-up Medthings. Mobili combines portability, automated dose dispensing and real-time monitoring, facilitating a more manageable medication regimen for chronic patients.
 This research project aims to explore the effectiveness of Mobili on medication adherence among chronic multimorbidity patients and its adaptability in a different health system. Achieving these aims will provide valuable insights into the deployment of technology-driven interventions in actual healthcare settings, potentially transforming digital adherence solutions for chronic patients. The CFIR 2.0 Implementation Research framework will guide the development of the research tasks.
 The project comprises four tasks:
 1. Project management and dissemination;
 2. Training of participating pharmacists, and collection of feedback on adaptability to the Portuguese context, through focus groups prior to the implementation of the intervention;

title: Data Management Plan for SmartSortMag
desc: This Data Management Plan (DMP) is for the project SmartSortMag: Machine Learning-Guided Identification and Recycling of Rare-Earth Permanent Magnets , which aims to develop a scalable, fully integrated waste-to-value machine learning-guided sorting device prototype that combines real-time X-ray fluorescence (XRF) sensing with data-driven classification of permanent magnets. By building a comprehensive experimental dataset and training supervised learning algorithms, the new technology will enable accurate identification of magnet types—including sintered, bonded, and nanocrystalline hot pressed Nd-Fe-B—directly on a sorting line. The output will inform robotic actuators to sort materials for optimal downstream recycling. title: Capacity building in genomic epidemiology of viral threats through expansion of INSaFLU and training provision
desc: The genetic characterization and surveillance of viral evolution is an urgent need at a global level in the context  of continuous emergence of viral threats, as recently observed in SARS-CoV-2 and mpox epidemics. The  existence of turnkey bioinformatics solutions covering all aspects of sequence data analysis is still an unmet  necessity. INSaFLU provides a user-friendly web-based solution enabling researchers with little training in  bioinformatics to perform multi-step computational analyses, starting from raw sequencing data. We have been  expanding the routine-oriented INSaFLU to include a  metagenomics viral pathogen detection module when the  viral threat is unknown. INSaFLU will also be expanded with novel reporting tools facilitating data interpretation  and, ultimately, public health decision-making. This project aims at supporting the continuous upgrade of the  existing “surveillance-oriented” component and the novel metagenomics virus identification module, as well as  ongoing and upcoming national and international training activities of INSaFLU. This support of the  development and training activities is expected to be essential to strengthen the functional and  computational  performance of the INSaFLU platform, ensuring that it can offer efficient services (for virus detection and  monitoring) to the scientific community at national and global scale, contributing to an enhanced capacity  building and preparedness for the prevention and control of viral infectious diseases.

title: Hybrid Graphene-Membrane Systems for Energy-Efficient Water Purification and Disinfection
desc: Latvia's wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) face mounting challenges from persistent contaminants such as pharmaceuticals, PFAS, and microplastics—pollutants inadequately removed by conventional treatment methods. National studies have found diclofenac and PFOS concentrations exceeding regulatory thresholds, alongside significant microplastic loads in effluents. These contaminants threaten local ecosystems and contribute to the degradation of the Baltic Sea, prompting urgent action in line with the HELCOM Baltic Sea Action Plan. This project proposes a modular, high-efficiency hybrid treatment system integrating three advanced technologies: (1) granular activated carbon (GAC) optimized for PFAS and pharmaceutical adsorption, (2) graphene oxide membranes with nanochannel control for the removal of microplastics and trace organics, and (3) UV-LED photocatalysis for energy-efficient disinfection. Building on prior successful applications in industrial and drinking water treatment, the project aims to design, fabricate, and pilot-test a scalable system in a Latvian WWTP. Methodologies include adsorption and filtration performance assessments, membrane characterization (SEM/AFM), and energy-use benchmarking of the UV-LED system. The integrated prototype targets >90% removal efficiencies, reduced energy costs, and alignment with EU and HELCOM environmental directives. This innovation aims to provide a cost-effective, sustainable solution for upgrading Latvia's municipal wastewater infrastructure and supporting broader regional water quality improvement.

title: Photothermally Enhanced Hydrogel-Based Thermoelectrochemical Cells for Stable, Passive Harvesting of Low-Grade Heat
desc: Low-grade waste heat (<100 °C) is an abundant yet underutilized energy resource due to its low exergy and the inefficiency of conventional conversion technologies under small temperature gradients and passive operation. Here, a photothermally enhanced thermoelectrochemical cell (PTEC) is reported, enabled by a high–ionic-conductivity double-network hydrogel electrolyte incorporating a guanidinium-boosted ferro/ferricyanide redox couple. Integration of photothermal carbon electrodes with a quasi-solid architecture establishes stable temperature gradients under both thermal and solar excitation, without active cooling or liquid electrolytes. The PTEC delivers an instantaneous thermopower of 4.5 mV K⁻¹ and a normalized power density of 5 mW m⁻² K⁻² under passive cooling, surpassing prior hydrogel-based thermoelectrochemical cells and approaching state-of-the-art liquid systems. Long-term operation reveals diffusion-limited decay that stabilizes at steady current densities, with impedance analysis identifying mass transport as the dominant bottleneck. Pulsed-load operation mitigates ion depletion, enhancing cumulative charge extraction by 2.5× and average power by >60% relative to continuous discharge. A nine-cell array directly recharges an electrochemical system using only low-grade heat ( ). This work elucidates key mechanisms governing sustained performance and demonstrates a robust, scalable platform for passive harvesting of ubiquitous low-grade heat toward self-powered distributed electronics.

title: JuDDGES (Judicial Decision Data Gathering, Encoding and Sharing) DMP CHIST-ERA
desc:
This document corresponds to the Data Mangement Plan for the JuDDGES (Judicial Decision Data Gathering, Encoding and Sharing) project and aims to apply FAIR principles to data and software produced. It will be updated regularly, at least every semester until the end of the project. Please note that this DMP follows the CHIST-ERA model using the ARGOS tool. Some questions are open-ended and others are closed, with multiple or single choice answers, which explains why some answers are short and lack context. The overall goal of the JuDDGES project is to harness state-of-the-art Natural Language Processing & Human-In-The-Loop technologies to provide legal researchers with new Open software and tools that enable extensive, flexible and on-going meta-annotation capability (both automated and employing domain experts in-the-loop). This capability is applied to legal records/judgments from criminal courts across jurisdictions with varied legal constitutions (Poland, England & Wales). 
 The project is organized into 4 WPs :  WP1: Project management WP2: Gathering and Human Encoding of Judicial Decision Data WP3: NLP and HITL Machine Learning Methodological Development WP4: Open science practices & engaging early career researchers More information here:  https://juddges-project.eu/ Candice Fillaud and Chérifa Boukacem-Zeghmouri (Université Lyon 1) written and compiled this DMP on ARGOS. Regarding the Polish data and software, Lukasz Augustyniak, Albert Sawczyn and Jakub Binkowski (Wrocław University of Science and Technology) provided the information. The UK data and software were provided by Santosh Tirunaguri and David Windridge (Middlesex University).

desc: This Data Management Plan (DMP) outlines the data lifecycle for the computational project detailing the origin and evolution of complex genomic rearrangements in pancreatic cancer. The purpose of this DMP is to define the protocols for securely transferring, processing, and managing sensitive human genomic data across a meta-cohort of 1,000 Pancreatic Cancer Whole-Genome Sequencing (WGS) samples utilizing the Portuguese National Advanced Computing Network (RNCA). It details the strict 'stage, process, and prune' batching strategy implemented to comply with HPC storage quotas (50 TB max), ensures strict adherence to external Data Access Committee (DAC) regulations regarding the secure deletion of raw patient files, and establishes the framework for publishing aggregated, non-identifiable analytical results in accordance with FAIR and Open Science principles.

Project summary: Forest4LV aims to enhance innovative forest management and new forest services, products and technologies in Latvia. Knowledge gaps regarding multipurpose management will be covered by standardized, complex, experimental assessment of survival, growth, quality, biodiversity and adaptation of forest. It will ensure integrity and coherence of the tasks and findings with pioneering European research in climate-smart forestry, and provide input for scenario modelling system. Interdisciplinary, holistic, stakeholder-input-based, agile socio-economic assessment of forest management scenarios (including climate change mitigation / substitution) will be the basis of the recommendations for policy and elaborated sustainability practices of forest sector actors. It will include solutions for rational use of forest resources in mechanical processing and biorefinery, advancing low-carbon economy. Innovative solutions for wood construction and use of wood materials will be explored, the valorisation of forest industry side streams will be addressed, and new biological, chemical and polymer material production technologies will be developed, thereby contributing to achievement of climate goals and economic growth. Young and upcoming researchers will be elucidated in methods and findings of holistic assessment of the effects arising in value chain from forest to end-products.

At the end of the project, the dataset will be archived in accordance with FAIR principles and deposited in the DataverseLV research data repository, thereby promoting transparency, reproducibility of research, and adherence to Open Science principles.

These alarming changes in biodiversity and ecosystem health present significant societal challenges. Meise Botanic Garden’s Science Strategy 2026-2035 outlines our commitment to addressing these challenges through innovative scientific research leveraging our invaluable collections and by raising public awareness about the critical importance of plant diversity. To address the societal challenges of the 21st century and demonstrate how our scientific research contributes to overcoming them, we have defined ten research ambitions for the period 2026–2035. The first five ambitions focus on what we will investigate and they are each aligned with a specific societal challenge. 1. Safeguarding the Belgian flora: maintaining our leading role as an expertise centre for the documentation and conservation of the Belgian flora. 2. Contributing to global conservation challenges: monitoring and conserving threatened species and vulnerable ecosystems globally, and in tropical Africa and Europe in particular. 3. Taking on global change challenges for plant diversity: contributing to addressing global environmental challenges by documenting and studying the factors most prominently threatening plant diversity. 4. Understanding and recording biodiversity: expanding our leadership in taxonomic research, to ensure that the foundational knowledge of biodiversity continues to underpin global conservation and sustainable development efforts. 5. title: Strategie Onderzoek, Plantentuin Meise, 2026-2035
desc: De plantendiversiteit wordt steeds meer bedreigd door verlies van leefgebied als gevolg van veranderend landgebruik, overexploitatie, vervuiling, de verspreiding van invasieve soorten en klimaatverandering. Deze alarmerende veranderingen in biodiversiteit en gezondheid van ecosystemen brengen aanzienlijke maatschappelijke uitdagingen met zich mee. De Strategie Onderzoek 2026-2035 van Plantentuin Meise schetst onze inzet om deze uitdagingen aan te pakken door innovatief wetenschappelijk onderzoek, gebruikmakend van onze waardevolle collecties, en door het publieke bewustzijn te vergroten over het cruciale belang van plantendiversiteit. Om de maatschappelijke uitdagingen van de 21e eeuw aan te pakken en te laten zien hoe ons wetenschappelijk onderzoek bijdraagt aan het overwinnen daarvan, definieerden we tien onderzoeksambities voor de periode 2026–2035. De eerste vijf ambities richten zich op wat we zullen onderzoeken en zijn elk afgestemd op een specifieke maatschappelijke uitdaging. 1. Veilig stellen van de Belgische flora: het behouden van onze leidende rol als expertisecentrum voor de documentatie en het behoud van de Belgische flora. 2. Bijdragen aan wereldwijde uitdagingen voor natuurbescherming: monitoring en bescherming van bedreigde soorten en kwetsbare ecosystemen wereldwijd, en in tropisch Afrika en Europa in het bijzonder. 3. Aanpakken van de uitdagingen op vlak van plantendiversiteit in een wereld in verandering: bijdragen aan het aanpakken van wereldwijde milieuproblemen door het documenteren en bestuderen van de factoren die de plantendiversiteit het meest bedreigen. 4. Begrijpen en documenteren van biodiversiteit: het versterken van onze leidende positie in taxonomisch onderzoek om ervoor te zorgen dat fundamentele kennis van biodiversiteit de basis

title: السياسة الفرنسية الاستعمارية في لبنان بين عامي (1918-1936)
desc: Abstracr: This study examines the French colonial policy in Lebanon between 1918 and 1936, analyzing France’s strategies in managing Lebanese territories following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire. The research explores the political, administrative, economic, and military aspects of the French Mandate, as well as its impact on internal stability, sectarian relations, and the development of Lebanese institutions. The study is divided into four chapters: the historical background and the fall of the Ottoman Empire, administrative and economic policies, military and diplomatic policies, and the effect of the French mandate on Lebanese society and governance. The findings reveal that the French Mandate reshaped central authority, established new administrative structures, but also reinforced sectarian divisions and local resistance. The study offers recommendations for a deeper understanding of the colonial legacy on Lebanon’s political and social development.   ملخص: يهدف هذا البحث إلى دراسة السياسة الفرنسية الاستعمارية في لبنان بين عامي 1918 و1936،  وتحليل استراتيجيات فرنسا في إدارة الأراضي اللبنانية بعد انهيار الدولة العثمانية. يتناول البحث الجوانب السياسية، الإدارية، الاقتصادية، والعسكرية للانتذاب الفرنسي، بالإضافة إلى أثر هذه   السياسات على الاستقرار الداخلي، العلاقات الطائفية، وتطوير المؤسسات اللبنانية.   يتضمن البحث أربعة فصول، حيث يبدأ باستعراض الخلفية التاريخية وسقوط الدولة العثمانية، ثم  دراسة السياسات الإدارية والاقتصادية، والسياسات العسكرية والدبلوماسية، وأخيراً تحليل أثر الانتذاب الفرنسي على المجتمع اللبناني ونظام الحكم.   أظهرت نتائج البحث أن الانتذاب الفرنسي أعاد تشكيل السلطة المركزية في لبنان، ورأى نظاماً إداريّاً جديداً، لكنه أيضاً ساهم في تعزيز الانقسامات الطائفية والمقاومة المحلية.

title: Unveiling molecular determinants and developmental niches for GdIgA+ B cell differentiation in IgA nephropathy
desc: This project aims to investigate the molecular determinants and developmental niches that drive the differentiation of galactose-deficient IgA1 (GdIgA1)-expressing B cells in IgA nephropathy (IgAN), an autoimmune kidney disease. The study focuses on identifying the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the production of pathogenic GdIgA1 antibodies, which are central to disease pathogenesis. To achieve this, multiple experimental approaches will be employed, including flow cytometry, single-cell transcriptional profiling, and confocal microscopy of mucosa- associated lymphoid tissue (MALT), particularly Peyer’s patches. These approaches will generate diverse datasets, including high-dimensional cytometry data, gene expression profiles, and imaging data. In addition, in vitro experiments using sorted B cell cultures and Peyer’s patch modeling will be conducted to mechanistically test factors that influence B cell activation, class switching, and differentiation into antibody-secreting cells. The project will generate both raw and processed datasets, including quantitative measurements, sequencing data, and annotated microscopy images. The data will be used to characterize differences between IgAN patients and healthy controls, with a focus on identifying key pathways and environmental cues that promote GdIgA1 production. All datasets will be organized, documented, and stored in accordance with FAIR data principles to ensure accessibility, reproducibility, and long-term usability.

title: भारतीय राजनीति में महिलाओं का राजनीतिक सशक्तिकरण: महिला आरक्षण विधेयक का मूल्यांकन

title: Affordable Sorting Validation for Accessible Stem Cell Therapy (DEPCELL)
desc: This Data Management Plan covers the data, software, AI models, analysis scripts, reports and metadata generated in the DEPCELL project. The project validates a label-free dielectrophoresis (DEP) sorting approach for viable adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (AD-MSCs) linked to telomere status, combined with AI-enabled quality control under GMP-like conditions to support accessible stem cell therapy under the Hospital Exemption pathway. Experimental data will be documented in standardised formats, stored in controlled RTU environments, and non-sensitive outputs will be made openly available in line with FAIR principles.

title: Synthesis of substituted heterocycles via electrophile addition - 1,2-silyl shift - cyclization domino process
desc: The work is dedicated to the development of new synthetic methodology, which allows to get various heterocyclic compounds with highly functionalized olefin side chain. Such compounds has potential application in pharmacy. The methodology is based on 1,2-migration of silicon in propargyl silanes attacked by electrophiles. After electrophilic addition to triple bond and consequent silyl group shift, the relatively stable allylic cation is formed. It can further react with inner nucleophiles providing cyclic compounds. This research is focused on the formation of chiral products what is crucial for biological activity of the potential drug. Three strategies to enantioselective cyclization were proposed: Desymmetrization strategy. Starting material is symmetric and contains 2 nucleophilic groups which are differentialized by chiral catalysis. Enantiospecific hypothesis. Attempt to synthesis of chiral starting material with assumption that cyclization proceeds by a concerted mechanism. Enantioselective strategy. Synthesis of racemic starting material and accent on stabilization of allyl cation transition state - if cyclization proceeds by a stepwise mechanism.

 The research is dome experimentally in fundamental science - chemistry. It will experimental research determine the reactivity of sulfur dioxide with various zwitterions. The obtained results will be used to create new methods for the synthesis of sulfur-containing organic compounds, which will be applicable in organic synthesis laboratories and industry. title: The Influence of Microbiome in Celiac Disease Using a Human iPSC-derived Celiac-disease-on-chip Model
desc: Coeliac disease (CeD) is an autoimmune disorder affecting approximately 1% of the global population. It is primarily triggered by gluten ingestion in genetically predisposed individuals, 90% of whom carry the HLA-DQ2 or HLA-DQ8 alleles, resulting in villous atrophy in the small intestine. Although genetic predisposition is well-characterized, the contribution of the gut microbiome to CeD pathogenesis remains insufficiently understood. The aim of the project is to elucidate the role of the microbiome in CeD using an advanced human iPSC-derived coeliac-disease-on-chip (CeDOC) model. The study will involve (1) isolation and sequencing of microbiota from healthy donors and CeD patients, (2) assembly of the CeDOC model using intestinal organoids, endothelial, and myeloid cells derived from CeD patients (3) co-culturing microbiota within the CeDOC system. The expected outcomes include novel insights into microbiome-driven modulation of gut barrier function and immune responses, with potential implications for therapeutic innovation.

title: Impact of Nanoplastic Particles on Intestinal Epithelium Health Using a Vascularized Gut-on-aChip Model
desc: Nanoplastics (NPLs), small plastic particles formed from the environmental breakdown of larger plastics, are known bioavailable contaminants. Their size enables them to cross biological barriers, interact with epithelial and immune cells, and transport toxic additives and biofilm-forming microbes. These properties highlight the urgent need to understand their effects on human health, particularly in the gastrointestinal tract (GI), a primary site of exposure through ingestion.  Despite mounting evidence linking NPLs to health issues like immune response and inflammation, their impact on gut health using physiologically relevant models remains poorly characterised. The objective of the project is to develop a novel proof-of-principle gut-on-chip model to evaluate the impact and toxicity of NPLs on gut health, focusing on bioaccumulation, translocation, and barrier integrity at the endothelium, epithelium, mucus and immune interface.

title: A Unified Chronos Framework for Structure Formation: Discrete Geometry, Stability Selection, and Time-Field Evolution
desc: This work presents a unified framework for structure formation across physical systems by addressing a key limitation in conventional approaches: geometry alone does not uniquely determine structure. Recent results demonstrate that systems sharing identical geometric constraints—such as metric and curvature—can yield distinct configurations. This reveals an underdetermination problem in which geometry defines possible states but does not explain which configuration is ultimately realized. To resolve this, we introduce a three-layer framework: Geometry defines the space of admissible configurations Stability, governed by the dimensionless constant χ, filters viable structures A scalar time field Θ(x,t) governs system evolution and selects the realized configuration through memory-dependent dynamics The time field introduces nonlocal temporal effects, allowing prior states to influence present evolution via phase-dependent feedback. This provides a mechanism for how systems transition, stabilize, and settle into specific structures. This framework unifies structure formation across scales, from atomic bonding and phase transitions to biological systems and cosmological structure. It offers a pathway for resolving ambiguities in systems where geometry alone is insufficient and highlights the role of temporal evolution as a fundamental selection mechanism.

title: Bridging the Cultural Divide: Strategies for Rural Families to Curate Digital Cultural Consumption for Youth / Kultūras plaisas mazināšana: lauku ģimeņu stratēģijas jauniešu digitālā kultūras patēriņa prakšu veidošanā
desc: The purpose of the data management plan for the project "Bridging the Cultural Divide: Strategies for Rural Families to Curate Digital Cultural Consumption for Youth" is to document and preserve the datasets collected during fieldwork with families. The aim of the study is to explore strategies for shaping digital cultural consumption in rural families and to identify effective approaches for promoting high-quality cultural participation among young people in the digital environment. The research design is based on digital ethnography, combining the researcher’s engagement with the family and the family’s own self-directed data collection in the digital environment through a mobile ethnography app.  The datasets include five types of data:  1) participants’ self-assessment questionnaires; 2)  interview and focus group transcripts; 3)  mobile ethnography data; 4)  contextual assessment data, including the evaluation of the family’s material objects, the cultural opportunities available in their place of residence, and cultural activities carried out to date; and 5)  the researcher’s fieldwork notes.

title: Data Management Plan for the Project "Practical applications and limitations of quantum search"
desc: This data management plan covers the data collected, generated and maintained during the course of the project ``Practical applications and limitations of quantum search'' of the 1.1.1.9 Research application No 1.1.1.9/LZP/2/25/206 of the Activity ``Post-doctoral Research''. In this project we plan to find novel methods of quantum search techniques by developing new algorithms and data structures for practical problems with various real-world applications. The main goal is to utilize various fundamental quantum search frameworks to provide new implementable quantum algorithms with provable quantum advantage over the classical (deterministic and probabilistic) algorithms, with outlook to the near-future quantum devices. The secondary goal is to give provable limitations for cases where the quantum improvement is impossible or limited.

title: Data Management Plan for "From Whispering Gallery Mode Doped Microspheres to Photonic Integrated Circuits for Advanced Next-Generation Applications"
desc: This Data Management Plan (DMP) covers the data that will be collected while implementing the project No. 1.1.1.9/LZP/2/25/190 "From Whispering Gallery Mode Doped Microspheres to Photonic Integrated Circuits for Advanced Next-Generation Applications" (hereinafter referred to as the Project). The aim of the Project is to investigate doped whispering gallery mode microspheres and tantalum pentoxide photonic integrated circuits' potential for lasing, optical frequency comb generation, and other advanced photonic applications. Planned research outputs of the Project are experiment raw data, experiment metadata, analysed data, deliverable data reports. All research data collected as part of the Project is owned by the University of Latvia. The project leader of the Project will take responsibility for the collection, management, and sharing of the research data. The aim and purpose of the DMP is to detail and guarantee the preservation of the data and documents collected during the Project, as well as any results derived from it. Proper data management - recording of collected data, storage and dissemination of the results - is important to ensure data collected for the Project is safely secured over its life cycle. The DMP includes multiple ways to responsibly manage the data.

title: Revealing the complexities of the pituitary tumor microenvironment via single cell and spatial transcriptomic sequencing (Nr. lzp-2025/1-0304)
desc: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are the most common intracranial tumors, yet they rarely metastasize. Pituitary tissue exhibits plasticity, but the mechanisms that prevent cancer development are unclear. This study will use spatial transcriptomics and in vitro cell experiments to investigate SF1-line PitNETs, ​​cell line models, and cancer cells. Objectives: 1) to identify spatial features that prevent malignancy by analyzing cell interactions, cell types, and pituitary plasticity; 2) to investigate the clinical applicability of markers from spatial transcriptomics data of gonadotropic PitNETs by comparing PitNETs with other tumors, searching for new therapeutic targets, and functionally investigating recent findings in the literature. 3) Perform integrated data analysis by linking spatial cell distribution to tumor cell composition and identifying clinical group, lineage and PitNET-specific localizations, biomarkers and common trends compared to other groups as well as reference data including PitNET, cancer and other neuroendocrine tumors, and take into account genetic background in this analysis. Functional experiments will use RNantisense A to investigate the role of genes recently identified in the literature and validate the novel findings of this project to advance the understanding of therapeutic targets for SF1 lineage PitNET. The project aims to uncover PitNET biology, improve treatments and provide information to other cancer research.

title: The Role of Extracellular Vesicle-Mediated snoRNA Transfer in Breast Cancer Progression
desc: Breast cancer (BC) is one of the most common  types of cancer in women, and in order to  effectively treat and control it, a better  understanding of its molecular mechanisms is  essential. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are small  particles  enclosed with  phospholipid bilayer that  can contain RNA, DNA, proteins, lipids and other  molecules, and  serve as a crucial mechanism for  intercellular communication. In previous studies,  we have  demonstrated that EVs derived from breast  and prostate cancer patients contain snoRNAs and  snoRNA- derived small RNAs (sdRNAs), while  in  plasma EVs from healthy controls  the level of  these  molecules  was  much lower. Additionally, the levels of 23 snoRNAs  dec reased  after surgery, suggesting  they originated from tumor- associated cells, and 13  snoRNAs were linked to poor responses to  neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The goal of this project is to explore  the  functions  of selected  snoRNAs / sdRNAs in  BC  development  and pr ogression. This will be achieved by  investigating the significance of these snoRNAs in  breast cancer cell lines through snoRNA  knockdown or overexpression, a nd the effects will  be analyzed by long- read and direct RNA sequencing. Furthermore, we will assess  the  transfer of EV- encapsulated snoRNAs to the tumor  microenvironment and their impact on the cells  within this environment. Gaining such insights  could open new possibilities for targeted drug  therapies and provide potential biomarkers to aid in  both ear ly tumor diagnosis and prognosis.

title: Economics of Happiness in Urban Environment: the case of European cities
desc: Improving urban quality of life is now increasingly at the top of the political agenda of modern cities. However, right policy treatment requires a thorough analysis and correct diagnosis. This project aims to create a modern and powerful urban quality of life analysis system which could be used as analytical base by lagging European cities to converge towards their peers. It provides a systematic assessment of the various quality of life dimensions – safety and trust, environment and infrastructure, urban governance, employment and poverty. Project is a quantitative research in Economics, with knowledge spillovers to Data Science, Sociology and Anthropology. It employs various hard and soft data sources, including Eurobarometer and Numbeo surveys. Scientific results will be disseminated via four original scientific articles, published Open Access and indexed in Web of Science and Scopus databases. Moreover, results will be presented in at least six public dissemination events, which are expected to deepen a cooperation with Riga City Council, other public institutions, business and NGOs. Extensive discussions with academic staff and incorporation of project into study process would foster capacity of a scientific team, further strengthened by international collaboration and knowledge sharing via membership in global academic societies. At the end of this project, a scientific team should be capable to design two new project applications, thus, enhancing the competitiveness of the University of Latvia in the long term.

title: AI-designed high-resolution 14N solid-state NMR for characterization of biological molecules.
desc: An atomic-level description of biomolecular 3D structure is vital for understanding disease mechanisms and designing new drugs. Solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a powerful method for analyzing the molecular structure and dynamics of biological solids, such as fibrils, viral capsids, and membrane proteins, which are associated with the progression of various diseases. However, obtaining high-quality structures requires high-resolution NMR spectra, which traditionally demand expensive and often impractical isotopic labeling of samples. This project will develop high-sensitivity, high-resolution solid-state NMR methods based on nuclei (1H and 14N) with nearly 100% natural abundance, enabling the study of label-free biomolecules. Until now, conventional NMR method development has failed to provide spectroscopic solutions for achieving high-resolution 14N spectra due to significant quadrupolar broadening. This project will leverage recent breakthroughs in artificial intelligence (AI) to aid in the design of NMR pulses capable of orientation-selective excitation, resulting in high-resolution 14N spectra. Success in this project will redefine biomolecular analysis, providing important insights into biomolecular properties and paving the way for the investigation of previously elusive biological systems.

The figure data include tabulated spectra, stacked transmission profiles, ionization-rate curves, optical-depth-ratio comparison curves, gas-overdensity curves, near/far gas-overdensity-ratio curves, and error profiles, with accompanying metadata and figure-specific README files. The parent DESI quasar and Lyα-forest data products are publicly available through the DESI DR1 release, including the DESI DR1 Lyα forest catalog. This deposit provides only the derived data products used in this work and does not re-distribute the full parent catalogs. Plotting/reproduction scripts are not included. title: PREVENTIVE APPLICATION OF SINGLE-USE NEGATIVE PRESSURE WOUND THERAPY (sNPWT) IN THE POSTOPERATIVE COURSE OF RADIOTREATED LIMB SARCOMA (PRALISS)
desc: Soft tissue sarcomas are a rare and heterogeneous group of solid tumors of mesenchymal origin that account for only 1% of all adult malignancies (AIOM 2021). Wide surgical excision of the tumor, with appropriate negative margins, is the mainstay treatment of localized STS, while neoadjuvant radiotherapy (nRT) – with or without chemotherapy – is recommended in selected high-grade STS (G2-G3) to reduce the stage of large tumors and achieve function-sparing radical excision. nRT may reduce tumor volume and/or make the pseudocapsule thicker and acellular, decreasing the risk of recurrence and seeding during surgical manipulation (Sampath et al). nRT is usually administered in 25 fractions for a total dose of 45 Gy (long-term nRT), but recently short-term administration with hypofractionation in 6 fractions for a total of 36 Gy has been proposed, with comparable effects. Surgery is performed 4-8 weeks after long-term nRT or 2 weeks after short-term nRT (Gronchi et al). Side effects of radiotherapy develop from the first administration and depend on the radiosensitivity of the treated site and the extent of irradiation. These effects are most noticeable in tissues with high cell remodeling, so surgical wounds are particularly exposed to these risks. Short-term wound complications (such as dehiscence, delayed healing, infection) are described in 35% of cases after nRT in STS (AIOM 2021). The main causes can be attributed to cell death, tissue ischemia caused by thrombosis of small vessels, or alterations in inflammatory and tissue healing processes. title: IMPACT OF MUSCULOSKELETAL DISORDERS ON EMPLOYEES IN THE IT  INDUSTRY
desc: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) have become a growing  occupational health concern in the modern workplace,  particularly within the Information Technology (IT)  industry. Employees in this sector spend long hours working  on computers, often maintaining static postures and  performing repetitive movements. These working conditions  can place excessive strain on muscles, joints, and connective  tissues, leading to various musculoskeletal problems such as  back pain, neck strain, shoulder discomfort, and wrist  injuries. Over time, these disorders can significantly affect  employees’ physical health, productivity, and overall quality  of life. The increasing reliance on digital technologies and  sedentary work environments has contributed to the rising  prevalence of MSDs among IT professionals across the  world. These disorders not only cause physical discomfort  but also lead to reduced work efficiency, increased  absenteeism, and higher healthcare costs for organizations.  Understanding the causes, risk factors, and consequences of  musculoskeletal disorders in the IT industry is therefore  essential for promoting occupational health and well-being.  This study aims to analyze how workers in the IT sector are  affected by musculoskeletal disorders and to examine the  lifestyle and workplace factors that contribute to these  conditions. The paper also highlights the importance of  ergonomic practices, regular physical activity, and  workplace awareness programs to reduce the occurrence of  MSDs. desc:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) describes the handling of data generated within the research project focused on the development and evaluation of synbiotic ingredients and delivery systems based on locally available plant raw materials. title: Religious Perspectives on the Conceptions of Disability
desc: Religious Perspectives on the Conceptions of Disability Liju T. Varghese  Abstract The influence of religion on the human worldview is beyond definition. The value systems, belief doctrines, and ritual practices of religions have, through the process of social construction, determined the position of the human being in the world. Contemporary society’s perspectives and attitudes toward disability often trace their origins to the deeper recesses of collective consciousness. An inquiry into this collective consciousness frequently leads to religious traditions and teachings.Disability is a term that has undergone numerous transformations. Often referred to solely in terms of deficiency or defined by limitations, disability is a concept that has been nurtured within the cultural framework of diverse perspectives. Humanistic studies demonstrate that interventions and understandings around disability have been shaped within such varied cultural constructs.What is the underlying reason for the formation of such perspectives in society? Disability has been marked in different periods of public consciousness through religious and cultural influences. The role of persons with disabilities within the structure of society is unique. Through religious, historical, and literary representations of disability, its moral legitimacy and sense of justice have long been questioned. Any approach to studying social and cultural discrimination remains critically relevant. The objective of this study is to examine the discriminatory configurations present in conceptions of disability within the religions of India. Social attitudes toward persons with physical and mental differences are generally bound by tradition. In earlier times, disability was confined to narrow interpretations

title: Thermal structure of the Qaanaaq Ice Cap outlet glaciers, north-western Greenland
desc: The aim of the project is to investigate the thermal structure, ice thickness, surface topography, and drainage system of the three largest outlet glaciers of the Qaanaaq Ice Cap. Although peripheral glaciers are especially sensitive to climate change, contributing to sea level rise and serving as an important freshwater resource, they are typically studied only at the the Greenland Ice Sheet scale. The thermal regime of peripheral glaciers remains poorly understood, hindering reliable future projections. Within the scope of this project, two expeditions will be carried out in 2026 and 2027, during which ground-penetrating radar, unmanned aerial vehicles, and passive seismic methods will be used. The project will provide new knowledge about the current state of the glaciers, advancing understanding of Arctic glacier dynamics, their response to climate change, and their impact on the local Qaanaaq community. All collected data will be openly accessible and used both in scientific research and public outreach, supporting Arctic research and the dissemination of knowledge in Latvia, Greenland, and beyond.

The project consists of six interrelated sub-projects that correspond to the research tasks defined in sub-paragraph 6.1.1 of the Cabinet Order No. 559 of 12 September 2025. Each sub-project generates and analyses linguistic data of different types, including lexicographic, corpus-based, dialectological, and onomastic material. title: Historical Dictionary of Latvian Given Names (LAnDe project)
desc: The aim of the project Latvian Anthroponymic Desiderata: diachronic research of unexplored Latvian given names for global integration and open access (LAnDe) (No. zp-2025/1-0125, project lead Renāte Siliņa-Piņķe) is to bring Latvian personal name material into the international scholarly circle through the study of 13th to 16th century sources that have not been linguistically analysed so far. The plan is (1) to excerpt and systematise given names data from 20 to 25 sources or sets of sources dating from the 13th to 16th century, (2) to carry out a study on the development of Latvian given names during this period on the basis of the obtained material and scientific literature; (3) to publish the results of the study as open access in at least three articles and in a minimum of 300 entries of the electronic Historical Dictionary of Latvian Given Names (LPVV); (4) on the basis of the insights and research gaps identified, prepare and submit a new project application to a national research and development project competition, (5) to improve the search engine of LPVV and to develop an educational game. The planned project outputs: at least three Scopus articles, 300 entries in the LPVV (origin, historical development, source examples, parallel forms, etc.), a new project application, and a digital educational game. The overarching aim of the project is to ensure the continuity of the temporarily interrupted research on personal names in line with the National Language Policy Framework Plan 2021-2027, and to develop an innovative solution in the field of digital humanities that would allow for the development of further solutions in historical research on language.

desc: The project investigates the integration of pharmaceutical cocrystals into extrusion-based 3D printed solid dosage forms, aiming to improve the solubility, stability, and personalized delivery of  drugs through tailored geometries and controlled release profiles. title: SPERMFREE: integrated analytical workflow for cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-based assessment of testicular function in severe male infertility
desc: The Data Management Plan (DMP) describes how research data generated within the SPERMFREE project will be collected, processed, stored, protected, and preserved throughout the project lifecycle. The project will generate several types of data, including next-generation sequencing (NGS) data from seminal plasma cell-free DNA, derived bioinformatic datasets (e.g., fragmentomic profiles, microbial signatures, and inferred gene-expression features), and associated pseudonymized clinical metadata. Raw sequencing data and intermediate computational files will be processed and temporarily stored using the High-Performance Computing (HPC) infrastructure provided by the Riga Technical University (RTU) High-Performance Computing Center. This infrastructure supports large-scale genomic data processing and secure storage required for next-generation sequencing analyses. Curated datasets supporting scientific analyses and publications will be archived in the institutional RSU Dataverse repository to ensure long-term preservation and compliance with FAIR data principles. Sensitive patient-related information will remain pseudonymized and stored in secure institutional systems. The bioinformatic workflow developed in this project constitutes a potentially patentable analytical technology; therefore, the pipeline source code will be maintained in a private version-controlled repository accessible only to the project team. Public release of proprietary components will be considered after completion of intellectual property protection procedures.

title: Real-Time Infrastructure Monitoring System Using Digital Twin and AI-Based Computer Vision Technique
desc:
The research project is non-economic in nature, as the scientific and technological knowledge generated will be disseminated in line with public information objectives. The research activities carried out within the project fall under the category of industrial research.
 The evolution of digital twin technology, combined with IoT-based real-time monitoring, states a transformative approach to infrastructure management, especially in steel bridge. This study focuses on developing a real-time infrastructure monitoring system for existing steel bridges in Latvia. The aim is to detect structural changes in steel bridge, predict failures, and enable proactive maintenance through a continuous real-time AI-driven monitoring system. Sensors such as accelerometers, strain gauges, temperature probes and high-resolution cameras will be strategically installed to capture real-time data which will communicate through LoRaWAN to ensure minimal latency in data processing. A critical aspect of this study is the development of a digital twin, which serves as a dynamic, real-time virtual replica of the physical steel bridge in Latvia. This digital representation will be created using Building Information Modelling, integrating real-time sensor feeds for continuous monitoring. A dashboard will be developed to visualize the live status of the steel bridge behaviour, enabling engineers and decision-makers to monitor key parameters such as structural stress, environmental conditions, and potential anomalies etc. The system will be designed to provide automated alerts when abnormal conditions are detected, not only in real-time but foresee the future changes, allowing for immediate interference.

title: Between Risk and Hope: Demographic Change and (Return)Migration in Latvia Amid Russia's War in Ukraine
desc: Project "Between Risk and Hope: Demographic Change and (Return)Migration in Latvia Amid Russia’s War in Ukraine (Nr. VPP-IZM-Letonika-2025/1-0002)". The project explores demography, migration, and return migration within the context of current geopolitical, socio-economic, and regional changes in Latvia. It considers Russia’s war in Ukraine as a structural shock that alters how people in Latvia and its diaspora make decisions about family formation, emigration, return, and integration. Drawing on theories of risk society, ontological security, and hope/future imaginaries, it examines how perceived insecurity and future expectations influence demographic behaviour. The project consists of five substantive work packages: 1) civic “X-Day” imaginaries and their demographic implications; 2) fertility and family strategies amidst insecurity; 3) return migration potential in the Latvian UK diaspora; 4) media discourse on migration; 5) integration experiences of post-2022 Ukrainian refugees, along with recent Belarusian and Russian migrants. Using mixed methods, including a nationally representative survey, survey and conjoint experiments, participant observation, and in-depth interviews, the project will produce reusable datasets, academic publications, policy briefs, regional outreach events, and a book. By working with Latvia’s ministries responsible for demography, welfare, defence, diaspora, and integration, it will provide evidence-based recommendations to improve population resilience, return migration strategies, and demographic policy planning amid long-term geopolitical pressures.

title: Elimination of Rigid PU Foam Thermal Insulation Shortcomings by Developing Bio-based Composites with a Gas Permeability Barrier Effect (BARRIER),  Nr. lzp-2025/1-0404
desc: The synergistic research approach of the BARRIER project will result in the development of rigid polyurethane (PU) foam composite for efficient long-term thermal insulation. By the introduction of fillers into bio-based rigid PU foam matrix, a decreased gas permeability of low GWP blowing agent through polymer matrix will be achieved. It will be determined what factors of the polymer matrix chemical structure and filler nature influence the gas permeability. The BARRIER project results will allow the design of rigid PU foam thermal insulation with higher efficiency and prolonged service lifetime to be used in civil engineering and appliance industry sectors. The BARRIER will advance expertise in developing low permeability rigid PU foams and gaining a deep understanding of rigid PU foam composite ageing and the influence of fillers to reduce gas diffusivity.

title: Science Collections Strategy 2026-2035. Meise Botanic Garden.
desc: Meise Botanic Garden's Science Collections Strategy 2026–2035 outlines a plan for maintaining and enhancing the Garden's science collections to support scientific research, conservation, and public engagement over the next decade. With over 225 years of history, the Garden manages a diverse collection including living plants, seeds, herbarium specimens, molecular samples, library resources and archives. These collections are essential for understanding biodiversity, addressing challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and food security, and fulfilling international commitments, including the Global Biodiversity Framework and the EU Biodiversity strategy for 2030. Over the past decade, we have made significant progress in digitising our collections, with three million herbarium specimens accessible online via platforms like the Global Biodiversity Information Facility. Building further on these achievements, the strategy focuses on improving access, preservation, and the scientific relevance of our collections. The strategy also reaffirms our long-standing Central African partnerships, supporting the restoration and digitisation of key collections and strengthening regional capacity for biodiversity research. The strategy is guided by five key ambitions: 1. Strengthening the impact of our collections for research, conservation, and policymaking: Prioritising taxa and regions of expertise, adopting technologies such as DNA sequencing and artificial intelligence, and ensure collections meet research and conservation needs. 2. Securing the collections for future generations: Upgrading collection facilities, enhancing preservation standards, and implementing a unified collection management system. 3. Expanding global access to our collections and their data

Deze collecties zijn essentieel voor het begrijpen van biodiversiteit, het aanpakken van mondiale uitdagingen zoals klimaatverandering, verlies van biodiversiteit en voedselzekerheid, en het nakomen van internationale verplichtingen, waaronder het Global Biodiversity Framework en de EU-biodiversiteitsstrategie voor 2030. In het afgelopen decennium is aanzienlijke vooruitgang geboekt in de digitalisering van de collecties, met inmiddels drie miljoen herbariumspecimens die online toegankelijk zijn via platforms zoals de Global Biodiversity Information Facility. Voortbouwend op deze resultaten richt de strategie zich op het verder verbeteren van de toegankelijkheid, het duurzaam behoud en de wetenschappelijke relevantie van de collecties. De strategie bevestigt tevens onze langdurige partnerschappen in Centraal-Afrika, waarbij Plantentuin Meise bijdraagt aan de restauratie en digitalisering van belangrijke collecties en aan de versterking van regionale capaciteit voor biodiversiteitsonderzoek. title: Data management plan for Autism spectrum disorder social rehabilitation using smart sensory toys and psychological profiling
desc: The prevalence of autistic spectrum disorder (ASD) has significantly increased, symptoms manifesting in preschool educational environment. ASD is characterized by impaired social interaction, communication deficits, and repetitive behaviors. The severity and symptoms vary among children, complicating timely and accurate diagnosis. In Latvia social rehabilitation and education extend beyond diagnosis, aiming to understand the child's psychological profile and how they form relationships and communicate. Early intervention targeting cognitive, social, and behavioral development is crucial. Behavior and communication therapies, especially Social Behavioral Therapy enhance emotional regulation, social skills, and communication. Technological interventions, such as robot-assisted autism therapy, have proven effective, however, they are expensive and complex. Smart sensory toys present a simpler, cost-effective alternative, enhancing social rehabilitation without requiring special training for use. The project aims to develop a psychological profile for using smart sensory toys in social rehabilitation for children with ASD. The research methodology includes a case study, to analyze and adjust the toys and creates a comprehensive psychological profile, involving parents, specialists, and children with ASD. The study adheres to ethical standards, ensuring participants' well-being, autonomy, and privacy. The findings will be published, maintaining transparency and research integrity.

Tiks izmantots arheoloģisko izrakumu materiāls no teritoriāli dažādām apbedījumu vietām ar izpētei pieejamu antropoloģisko materiālu. Dzīves apstākļu un kvalitātes raksturojums balstīsies uz apbedījumu paleopatoloģisko izpēti, kā ari stabilo izotopu (diētas) un mikrobioma datiem. Projektā tiks realizēta inovatīva pieeja kapulauku iekšējās struktūras izpētē, līdztekus apbedīšanas tradīciju arheoloģiskajai izpētei, pielietojot molekulārās bioloģijas (DNS) un fizikāli ķīmiskās (izotopi, peptīdi) metodes. DNS analīzes tiks izmantotas gan atsevišķu indivīdu, gan apbedījumu grupu un populācijas ģenētiskajam raksturojumam, nosakot savstarpējo radniecību un izcelsmi. Savukārt izotopu analīzes sniegs informāciju gan par diētas atšķirībām starp indivīdiem un apbedījumu grupām, gan arī mobilitāti.
