desc: This document is the initial version of the Data Management Plan (DMP) for the research study (2025–2027), conducted within the Fundamental and Applied Research Programme under project No. LZP-2024/1-0616, "StAR: Labour Market Response to Shocks – Strategies for Adaptability and Resilience." The DMP will be managed as a living document using the Argos DMP tool, with significant updates periodically uploaded to Zenodo throughout the project's duration. Regular revisions will align with periodic project evaluations, or more frequently as necessary. The DMP outlines a comprehensive strategy for managing the data used during the StAR project. The project aims to advance scientific understanding of how labour markets respond to major economic shocks, with a specific focus on the Financial Recession, the Covid-19 pandemic, and the surge in energy prices following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. It also examines the determinants and evolution of the gender pay gap in Europe, the long-term effects of job displacement in Latvia, and the link between unemployment and transitions into entrepreneurship. In addition, the project investigates the role of firms and job mobility in shaping gender wage disparities in Latvia.  The StAR project relies exclusively on secondary, anonymised datasets accessed under strict confidentiality and legal agreements. These include harmonised microdata from EU-SILC and the Labour Force Survey for all EU Member States, Eurostat sector-level productivity statistics, matched employer-employee (MEE) administrative records compiled by the State Revenue Service (SRS) and managed by the Central Statistical Bureau (CSB). The primary hypothesis posits that reality is fundamentally a self-generating, computational process operating within a dynamic medium. Within this framework, a cornerstone concept is the identity of mass as intrinsic frequency. The research is precisely structured into three primary modules: the first module critically challenges the fundamental nature of spacetime as conceptualized by Special Relativity; the second module questions the axiomatic nature of particle properties as presented in early quantum theory; and the third module challenges the geometric interpretation of gravity in General Relativity. The overarching objective of this program is to demonstrate that the Autaxys framework is capable of comprehensively re-deriving the confirmed predictions of these existing theories from its own first principles, while simultaneously offering more parsimonious explanations for persistent cosmological anomalies, such as dark matter and dark energy. desc: For my work as a mathematics teacher, I am exposed to many questions from students about some mathematical rules and how to prove them. He said that he had watched a video on YouTube that said that the sum of the positive integers is a negative number and equals -1/12. I watched the video and the proof of addition of integers, and I am sorry to say that I tried to convince myself of this proof, but to no avail. Therefore, I wrote this research paper that discusses all the errors of scientists regarding the truth of addition of positive integers. And out of my belief that all universities around the world are beacons of knowledge, I put up some university logos to review my research paper. desc: Resumen Hibiscus sabdariffa , conocida como flor de Jamaica, es una planta ampliamente estudiada por su alto contenido de compuestos bioactivos con propiedades antioxidantes, antihipertensivas y hepatoprotectoras. En Ecuador, la región oriental presenta condiciones favorables para su cultivo, pero aún existen pocos estudios sobre su caracterización química y bioactividad. Esta revisión bibliográfica tiene como objetivo evaluar los principales compuestos bioactivos de  H. sabdariffa  producida en el Oriente ecuatoriano, sus propiedades funcionales y su potencial aplicación en la industria alimentaria y farmacéutica. Se realizó una búsqueda sistemática en bases de datos científicas como Scopus, ScienceDirect, PubMed y Google Scholar, seleccionando estudios publicados entre 2019 y 2024. Se analizaron los factores que influyen en la composición química de los cálices, así como los métodos de extracción más eficientes, destacándose la extracción asistida por ultrasonido y la extracción por calor. Los resultados indican que la concentración de antocianinas y polifenoles en  H. sabdariffa  varía según las condiciones agroecológicas y los métodos de procesamiento. Además, se identificaron limitaciones en la estabilidad de estos compuestos durante el almacenamiento de productos derivados, lo que sugiere la necesidad de optimizar las estrategias de conservación. Se concluye que  H. sabdariffa tiene un alto potencial para su aprovechamiento en Ecuador, pero es necesario continuar con estudios que permitan estandarizar sus procesos de producción y eva

title: Integración de la gobernanza de datos en la formación docente: Un modelo innovador en Eduplanet, Ecuador
desc: Resumen Este estudio investigó la integración de la gobernanza de datos en la formación docente en Eduplanet, enfatizando su capacidad para mejorar la calidad educativa y los procesos administrativos. El objetivo principal consistió en analizar la implementación del modelo DAMA como marco estratégico para fortalecer las competencias digitales del personal docente, optimizando tanto la eficacia pedagógica como la eficiencia administrativa. Se adoptó una metodología de enfoque mixto que combinó el análisis estadístico de datos cuantitativos, obtenidos mediante cuestionarios estructurados, con el análisis cualitativo derivado de entrevistas semiestructuradas realizadas a una muestra intencionada de 12 docentes. Los resultados evidenciaron una correlación positiva significativa entre las competencias en gobernanza de datos y la eficacia docente (r=0.98), así como con la eficiencia administrativa (r=0.78), destacando el impacto transversal de estas habilidades. Los hallazgos subrayan la importancia de implementar programas de formación diferenciados para reducir brechas entre niveles de experiencia y maximizar los beneficios del uso de datos en la enseñanza. Para Eduplanet, estas conclusiones refuerzan su posición estratégica como institución innovadora en Ecuador, proporcionando un marco replicable para la adopción de prácticas basadas en datos alineadas con estándares internacionales.

desc: Цей документ є офіційним шаблоном Плану управління дослідницькими даними (ПУДД) , затвердженим Бердянським державним педагогічним університетом (БДПУ) для використання в наукових проєктах. Шаблон розроблено відповідно до політики відкритої науки, принципів FAIR (Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability) і CARE (Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility, Ethics), а також міжнародних рекомендацій щодо якісного управління даними.  Шаблон містить: зручну структуру з покроковими інструкціями та прикладами; розділи, що охоплюють повний життєвий цикл дослідницьких даних (від джерел і форматів до етичних аспектів та поширення); орієнтованість як на природничі, так і соціогуманітарні дослідження; практичне застосування для аспірантів, дослідників і координаторів наукових проєктів. Шаблон є невід’ємною частиною політики університету з управління дослідницькими даними та використовується при поданні технічних завдань, реєстрацій наукових тем, а також у підготовці до грантових конкурсів.

title: Navigating Post-Exile: Transformations and Transitions in the Latvian Exile Community after 1991
desc: The project aims to explore the “post-exile” period of the Latvian exile community formed after World War II, highlighting its evolution following Latvia’s independence in 1991, when the “old exile” became part of the emerging diaspora. By examining the transformation of exile community identities, their relationships and ties to their homeland, the experiences of returnees, and the dynamics between the “old exile” and recent emigrants, the project will provide a nuanced understanding of the post-exile experience.  A multidisciplinary approach, integrating historical and biographical research methods, will offer insights into individuals’ sense of belonging and identity development during a time marked by significant migration in Latvia and globally.  The research is conducted within the Fundamental and Applied Research Programme project "Navigating Post-Exile: Transformations and Transitions in the Latvian Exile Community after 1991" (project No. LZP-2024/1-0114), funded by the Latvian Council of Science.

title: Livonic Dialect in Courland: Conception and Methodology of New Classification (LiviDo)
desc: The project “Livonic Dialect in Courland: Conception and Methodology of New Classification” (LiviDo) develops an appropriate methodology and uses research approaches that have so far been little known in Latvian dialectology (used mainly in sociolinguistics and geolinguistics) to develop a scientific concept for the delimitation of new boundaries of the Tamian subdialects and the evaluation of more appropriate terminology for naming this group of Livonic dialect. The research is based on the most recent dialectal data collected so far in the 21st century, and the project also aims to collect new dialectal data in the unexplored territory of the Tamian subdialects, especially in the borderline of the deep and the non-deep Tamian subdialects of the Livonic dialect, as well as in the transitional zone of the Livonic and the Couronic subdialects of the Central dialect. To reconstruct the dialectal data, early audio materials of the Courland Livonic dialect from the second half of the 20th century will be digitalized and analysed. The aim of the project: To create a new classification of the Livonic dialect spoken in Northern Courland, based on newer dialectal data collected in the 21st century and comparing them to oldest ones acquired in the second half of the 20th century. The Data Management Plan is developed in the framework of the Recovery and Resilience Facility project "Internal and External Consolidation of the University of Latvia" (No.5.2.1.1.i.0/2/24/I/CFLA/007), grant project “Livonic Dialect in Courland: Conception and Methodology of New Classification”, No LU-BA-PA-2024/1-0033.

title: Description of the Data Management Plan (DMP) for the Healthcare Pathways of Heart Failure Patients within the Spanish National Health System and its Impact on Health Outcomes (CONCEPT-HF) Project
desc: This dataset provides an in-depth Data Management Plan (DMP) for the CONCEPT-HF project, focusing on the healthcare pathways of heart failure (HF) patients within the Spanish National Health System and its impact on health outcomes.  It includes comprehensive data from HF patients admitted to public hospitals, detailing patient attributes such as comorbidities, healthcare interactions, prescribed medications, and outcomes like readmissions and mortality. The DMP highlights the secondary use of pseudonymized individual-level data sourced from primary care, hospital admissions, insurance registries, and electronic health records. The data is continuously managed and updated by regional health systems following a common data model specification to ensure consistency and reliability across the dataset. This model supports a federated approach to data analysis, with each region extracting and processing relevant data locally. Metadata and controlled vocabularies are emphasized to ensure data interoperability and reusability. The dataset is deposited in Zenodo, providing open access to researchers and healthcare professionals. The DMP also includes detailed information on repository details, data sharing policies, security measures, and ethical considerations, ensuring full compliance with data protection regulations. This dataset aims to facilitate research into the healthcare pathways of HF patients and improve health outcomes through informed decision-making. Keywords: heart failure, healthcare pathways, Spanish National Health System, health outcomes, data management plan, CONCEPT-HF, public health research

title: DMP: Analysis between Suicide and Happiness
desc: Context and methodology This dataset originates from the intersection of the scientific and statistical realms, spurred by a research initiative aiming to delve into the intricate relationship between suicide rates and happiness levels across various countries. The overarching domain of investigation or project that prompted the inception of this dataset is deeply entrenched in understanding the dynamics and potential correlations between these two societal phenomena. The paramount purpose of this dataset lies in its ability to unravel answers to the fundamental question: is there a discernible link between suicide rates and happiness levels? The analytical exploration of this dataset aspires to yield valuable insights that can illuminate underlying factors or trends associated with the complex interplay of suicide and happiness. As for the genesis of this dataset, it evolved through a meticulous amalgamation of information sourced from two distinct databases. While one of these databases had already been established, the other necessitated proactive research efforts to compile and integrate pertinent data. This amalgamation process not only facilitated the creation of a comprehensive dataset but also formed a robust foundation for subsequent analysis and research endeavors probing the correlation between suicide and happiness. Technical details The structure of this dataset is presented as a table with clearly identified titles and orderly arranged data. There are no abbreviations or elements that could cause confusion, contributing to an intuitive understanding of the information. title: DMP Factors that affect sleep efficiency
desc: This project has been created to analyze some data and through statistical procedures to obtain new data to answer some previously proposed questions. These answers help us to see if some factors recommended by health or popular beliefs have a scientific basis, and therefore to see if they affect people's sleep efficiency. Factors such as the benefits of physical activity or negative consequences such as coffee are contrasted and also some data differ between genders or whether people sleep the hours recommended by health. In addition, hours of deep sleep and light sleep are differentiated to directly address the problem of efficiency. By contrasting the different data in RStudio, we draw valid and scientifically based conclusions for the users of the sample. These data, from totally anonymous people, are tables in csv format that can be opened in different platforms, but I chose RStudio because it was the best to work with the data; but the document obtained with the answers to the research are in a pdf with its graphics included. No specific software is needed to open the dataset itself, since the obtained dataset and conclusions are in a pdf file, so everyone can easily open and understand the results of the experiment. In order to open the existing datasets to have already formed the data, you need an application that can open csv. The conclusions drawn are from a sample of specific data. To see the full credibility of these data it would be necessary to extrapolate, so when working with a similar but different database some conclusions could change, or when changing the significance level of the contrasts, but in general the data obtained are accurate and correspond to the sample given to try to answer the proposed questions.

This document will present the policies, principles and implemented measures to ensure the said compliance hereunder with the applicable personal data protection requirements, contextualized with an overview of relevant data flows and datasets occurring throughout the Project, and constitutes the core of the applicable detailed data protection policy for the Project.

title: CINECA Data Management Plan v2
desc: The overarching purpose of CINECA is to achieve federated human data interoperability between 10 existing cohorts from Canada, Europe and Africa which represent >1.4 million individuals. This will enable population scale genomic and biomolecular data access across international borders, accelerating research and improving the health of individuals resident across continents. This project will not generate novel data from human data, rather it relies on integrating existing resources which hold or store data to deliver new knowledge and innovation. All data access is determined by the existing data access committees (DACs) and the respective data processes for each dataset (Appendix 1 explains the process for accessing secondary use data for each cohort). The informed consent and ethics approvals for CINECA cohorts were documented in previous ethics deliverables and will be respected by this data management plan, which will be an integral part of the consortium’s Governance Framework. Given the international nature of this project, the data management plan is a component of Work Package 7 - Ethical and legal governance framework for transnational data-sharing. We note that all partners in the project have relevant national and/or international experience in acquiring, storing, analysing and sharing high complexity datasets and in the implementation of the FAIR principles for these resources.   The Data Management Plan (DMP) was developed based on the core requirements for DMPs as described by The Science Europe Practical Guide to the International Alignment of Research Data Management (https://www.scienceeurope.org). The DMP is a living document, expected to be updated during the lifetime of the project.
